history.insight: Combines a doubly linked list with a hash map to achieve O(1) get and put operations while maintaining access order for eviction.
Also known as the Tortoise and Hare algorithm, uses two pointers moving at different speeds (1 step and 2 steps) to detect cycles in linked lists in O(n) time and O(1) space.
DSU or Union-Find tracks elements partitioned into disjoint subsets. With path compression and union by rank, operations run in nearly O(1) amortized time (inverse Ackermann function α(n)).
Solves complex problems by breaking them into overlapping subproblems with optimal substructure. Memoization (top-down) and tabulation (bottom-up) eliminate redundant computation.
A tree data structure for storing intervals or segments, allowing querying range sum/min/max and point/range updates in O(log n) time.
Divides the search interval in half repeatedly on sorted collections, running in logarithmic time O(log n). Always watch out for integer overflow: use mid = low + (high - low) // 2.
A tree-like data structure used for efficient retrieval of keys in a dataset of strings, ideal for autocomplete and spell-checkers with O(L) lookup where L is word length.
Finds the single-source shortest path in weighted graphs with non-negative edges using a min-heap in O((V + E) log V) time.
Hash maps achieve average O(1) time complexity by mapping keys to bucket indices using a hash function. Collision resolution commonly uses chaining or open addressing (linear/quadratic probing).
